title: Find the Highest and Lowest Salary
description:
Return the highest and lowest salary across all employees **in a single row**.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `department`, `salary`

Return `max_salary` and `min_salary`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering',95000),(2,'Bob','Engineering',85000),(3,'Carol','Sales',70000),(4,'Dave','Sales',65000),(5,'Eve','Marketing',75000),(6,'Frank','HR',60000);
solution_sql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS max_salary, MIN(salary) AS min_salary FROM employees

test_cases.description: Single row with max_salary=95000 and min_salary=60000

hints: MAX() and MIN() can appear together in the same SELECT — both operate over all rows.
No GROUP BY needed here — this aggregates the entire table into a single result row.
explanation: When aggregate functions are used without GROUP BY, they collapse all rows into a single result. MAX(salary) = 95000 (Alice) and MIN(salary) = 60000 (Frank). Both values appear on the same output row.
